beats.speak: White's knight lands on E seven. It checks the king on G eight and attacks the rook on C eight at the same moment.

beats.label: The king must move
beats.say: Black has to deal with the check first. The king steps into the corner, to h8.
beats.speak: Black has to deal with the check first. The king steps into the corner, to H eight.

beats.label: The rook falls
beats.say: White's knight captures the rook on c8. One move made two threats, and a whole rook was won.
beats.speak: White's knight captures the rook on C eight. One move made two threats, and a whole rook was won.

beats.label: Pawns fork too
beats.say: Pawns can fork as well. Black's knights stand on d6 and f6, with one empty square between them.
beats.speak: Pawns can fork as well. Black's knights stand on D six and F six, with one empty square between them.

beats.label: One pawn, two knights
beats.say: White's pawn advances to e5, right between them. It attacks both knights at once.
beats.speak: White's pawn advances to E five, right between them. It attacks both knights at once.

beats.label: Why it works
beats.say: Neither knight can capture the pawn, and Black can move only one of them. White will capture the other one. Even if Black wins the pawn back, White has gained a knight, worth three, for a pawn, worth one.
beats.speak: Neither knight can capture the pawn, and Black can move only one of them. White will capture the other one. Even if Black wins the pawn back, White has gained a knight, worth three, for a pawn, worth one.

beats.label: The queen forks
beats.say: The queen moves in every direction, so she forks often. Look at Black's king on g8 and the rook on a8.
beats.speak: The queen moves in every direction, so she forks often. Look at Black's king on G eight and the rook on A eight.

beats.label: Check and attack
beats.say: White's queen goes to d5. She checks the king along one diagonal and attacks the rook along another.
beats.speak: White's queen goes to D five. She checks the king along one diagonal and attacks the rook along another.

beats.label: The rook falls again
beats.say: Black's king slips into the corner, to h8. White's queen takes the rook on a8, giving check again.
beats.speak: Black's king slips into the corner, to H eight. White's queen takes the rook on A eight, giving check again.

beats.label: Keep the forker safe
beats.say: A fork works best when the forking piece cannot simply be captured. Before you fork, check that the square you land on is safe.
beats.speak: A fork works best when the forking piece cannot simply be captured. Before you fork, check that the square you land on is safe.

beats.label: Check comes first
beats.say: A fork that includes a check is usually the strongest kind. Unless the forking piece can simply be taken, the opponent is busy with the check and cannot rescue the second target.
beats.speak: A fork that includes a check is usually the strongest kind. Unless the forking piece can simply be taken, the opponent is busy with the check and cannot rescue the second target.

beats.label: How to find forks
beats.say: Before each move, ask: can one of my pieces attack two valuable targets at once? Kings, queens and rooks make the best targets.
beats.speak: Before each move, ask: can one of my pieces attack two valuable targets at once? Kings, queens and rooks make the best targets.

beats.label: Your turn
beats.say: Now try it yourself against the computer. White's knight on g5 can fork two of Black's pieces. Find the fork, win material, and play on to win the game.
beats.speak: Now try it yourself against the computer. White's knight on G five can fork two of Black's pieces. Find the fork, win material, and play on to win the game.

practice.goal: Find the knight fork that wins material, then play on to win the game.

checkpoints.label: Fork two pieces and win material

hints: Look for a square where your knight attacks two valuable black pieces at once, and where no black piece can capture it.
Black's queen on d8 and rook on f8 are the targets. Which jump of your knight on g5 attacks both of them?
practice.offTrack: That move does not win material with a fork. Undo it: put your knight where it attacks two black pieces at once, then take the one Black cannot save.

mistakes.g5f7: The knight on f7 checks the king and attacks the queen, but Black's rook on f8 simply takes it. Undo it and fork from a safe square.

practice.success: Your knight attacked Black's queen and rook together. The queen escaped, so the knight took the rook: a rook, worth five, for at most a knight, worth three. Play on to win the game.

lessons.title: The Pin
teaches: A pin is an attack on a piece that cannot or should not move off its line, because a more valuable piece stands behind it.
In an absolute pin the piece behind is the king, so the pinned piece may not leave the line (a pinned knight can never move).
In a relative pin the pinned piece may move, but something valuable behind it would be lost.
Only bishops, rooks and queens can pin, because they move along lines.
Attack a pinned piece again, especially with a pawn: it cannot run away.

beats.label: Stuck in place
beats.say: A pin is an attack on a piece that cannot move off its line, or should not, because a more valuable piece stands behind it on the same line.
beats.speak: A pin is an attack on a piece that cannot move off its line, or should not, because a more valuable piece stands behind it on the same line.

beats.label: Making a pin
beats.say: White's bishop goes to b5 and attacks the knight on c6. Behind that knight, on the same diagonal, is Black's king on e8.
beats.speak: White's bishop goes to B five and attacks the knight on C six. Behind that knight, on the same diagonal, is Black's king on E eight.

beats.label: It cannot move
beats.say: If this knight stepped away, the bishop would be giving check, and the rules forbid that. A knight can never stay on its line, so this one is frozen.
beats.speak: If this knight stepped away, the bishop would be giving check, and the rules forbid that. A knight can never stay on its line, so this one is frozen.

beats.label: An absolute pin
beats.say: A pin against the king is called an absolute pin. The rules forbid the pinned piece to step off the line; at most it may slide along it or capture the pinner.
beats.speak: A pin against the king is called an absolute pin. The rules forbid the pinned piece to step off the line; at most it may slide along it or capture the pinner.

beats.label: Attack the pinned piece
beats.say: Now use the pin. White's pawn advances to d5 and attacks the knight. The knight cannot run, so White will capture it next move.
beats.speak: Now use the pin. White's pawn advances to D five and attacks the knight. The knight cannot run, so White will capture it next move.

beats.label: A pin to the queen
beats.say: Here White's bishop on g5 attacks the knight on f6. Behind the knight, on the same diagonal, stands Black's queen on d8.
beats.speak: Here White's bishop on G five attacks the knight on F six. Behind the knight, on the same diagonal, stands Black's queen on D eight.

beats.label: Allowed, but costly
beats.say: The rules let this knight move, since no king hides behind it. Yet moving it hands the queen to the bishop. We call this a relative pin: legal to move, but very costly.
beats.speak: The rules let this knight move, since no king hides behind it. Yet moving it hands the queen to the bishop. We call this a relative pin: legal to move, but very costly.

beats.label: The pawn joins in
beats.say: White's pawn advances to e5 and attacks the pinned knight. If the knight moves, the queen falls; if it stays, the pawn takes it.
beats.speak: White's pawn advances to E five and attacks the pinned knight. If the knight moves, the queen falls; if it stays, the pawn takes it.

beats.label: Material will fall
beats.say: Black cannot keep both the knight and the queen. A pinned piece attacked by a pawn is very often simply lost.
beats.speak: Black cannot keep both the knight and the queen. A pinned piece attacked by a pawn is very often simply lost.

beats.label: Pins along files
beats.say: Rooks and queens pin along files and ranks. Here White's rook on e1 pins Black's bishop on e6 to the king on e8.
beats.speak: Rooks and queens pin along files and ranks. Here White's rook on E one pins Black's bishop on E six to the king on E eight.

beats.label: Who can pin
beats.say: Only bishops, rooks and queens can pin, because they attack along lines. A knight, a pawn or a king cannot pin anything.
beats.speak: Only bishops, rooks and queens can pin, because they attack along lines. A knight, a pawn or a king cannot pin anything.

beats.label: Spotting pins
beats.say: Look for two enemy pieces on the same line, with the more valuable one behind. A bishop, rook or queen on that line can pin the front piece.
beats.speak: Look for two enemy pieces on the same line, with the more valuable one behind. A bishop, rook or queen on that line can pin the front piece.

beats.label: Using a pin
beats.say: When you pin a piece, attack it again, ideally with a pawn. Also check what the pinned piece was guarding, because it may no longer be able to help.
beats.speak: When you pin a piece, attack it again, ideally with a pawn. Also check what the pinned piece was guarding, because it may no longer be able to help.

beats.label: Your turn
beats.say: Now try it yourself against the computer. Black's knight on c6 stands on the same diagonal as Black's king. Pin it, attack it, and win material.
beats.speak: Now try it yourself against the computer. Black's knight on C six stands on the same diagonal as Black's king. Pin it, attack it, and win material.

practice.goal: Pin Black's knight to the king, attack the pinned piece, and win material.

checkpoints.label: Pin the knight, attack it, win material

hints: Pin the knight to its king with a piece that moves along that diagonal, then attack the pinned knight again, ideally with a pawn.
Your bishop on c4 can step onto the diagonal in front of the knight, and your pawn on d4 is one step from attacking c6.
practice.offTrack: That does not use the pin. Undo it: pin the knight on c6 to the king first, then attack it with a pawn so that it cannot run.

mistakes.d4d5: Attacking the knight before it is pinned lets it run, and from e5 it would attack your bishop. Undo it and pin the knight first.

practice.success: Your bishop pinned the knight and your pawn attacked it. The knight could not run without losing more, so your pawn took it: a knight for at most a pawn. Play on.

lessons.title: The Skewer
teaches: A skewer attacks a valuable piece that must move away, uncovering a piece behind it.
A skewer is like a pin turned round: the more valuable piece stands in front.
When a skewer gives check and the check cannot be blocked or the checking piece captured, the king must move and the piece behind falls.
Only bishops, rooks and queens can skewer, because they attack along lines.

beats.label: Front and back
beats.say: A skewer is an attack on a valuable piece that has to move away, so that a piece behind it can be captured.
beats.speak: A skewer is an attack on a valuable piece that has to move away, so that a piece behind it can be captured.

beats.label: Rook skewer
beats.say: White's rook slides to e2. It checks the king on e5, and behind the king, on the same file, stands Black's queen on e8.
beats.speak: White's rook slides to E two. It checks the king on E five, and behind the king, on the same file, stands Black's queen on E eight.

beats.label: The king must step aside
beats.say: Black must get out of check. Nothing can block the line or capture the rook, so the king has to step off the file.
beats.speak: Black must get out of check. Nothing can block the line or capture the rook, so the king has to step off the file.

beats.label: The king steps away
beats.say: Black's king steps aside, to f5.
beats.speak: Black's king steps aside, to F five.

beats.label: The queen falls
beats.say: White's rook captures the queen on e8. The skewer won a queen for nothing.
beats.speak: White's rook captures the queen on E eight. The skewer won a queen for nothing.

beats.label: A pin turned round
beats.say: Think of a skewer as a pin turned round. A pin traps a cheaper piece with a dearer one behind it. A skewer hits the dearer piece first, and it has to get out of the way.
beats.speak: Think of a skewer as a pin turned round. A pin traps a cheaper piece with a dearer one behind it. A skewer hits the dearer piece first, and it has to get out of the way.

beats.label: Bishop skewer
beats.say: Bishops skewer along diagonals. Black's king stands on f5, and further along the same diagonal is Black's rook on h7.
beats.speak: Bishops skewer along diagonals. Black's king stands on F five, and further along the same diagonal is Black's rook on H seven.

beats.label: Check on the diagonal
beats.say: White's bishop goes to d3 and checks the king. The rook on h7 is behind the king on the same diagonal.
beats.speak: White's bishop goes to D three and checks the king. The rook on H seven is behind the king on the same diagonal.

beats.label: The rook falls
beats.say: Black's king steps aside, to e5. White's bishop takes the rook on h7.
beats.speak: Black's king steps aside, to E five. White's bishop takes the rook on H seven.

beats.label: Skewer without check
beats.say: A skewer does not need a king. Here Black's queen stands on d4, and the rook on h8 is behind her on the long diagonal.
beats.speak: A skewer does not need a king. Here Black's queen stands on D four, and the rook on H eight is behind her on the long diagonal.

beats.label: Attack the queen
beats.say: White's bishop goes to b2 and attacks the queen. If the queen takes the bishop, White's rook on b1 takes her back.
beats.speak: White's bishop goes to B two and attacks the queen. If the queen takes the bishop, White's rook on B one takes her back.

beats.label: The queen leaves
beats.say: Black's queen escapes to d5. White's bishop takes the rook on h8.
beats.speak: Black's queen escapes to D five. White's bishop takes the rook on H eight.

beats.label: Who can skewer
beats.say: Only bishops, rooks and queens can skewer, because they attack along lines. A knight, a pawn or a king cannot.
beats.speak: Only bishops, rooks and queens can skewer, because they attack along lines. A knight, a pawn or a king cannot.

beats.label: Spotting skewers
beats.say: Look for two enemy pieces on one line with the more valuable one in front, especially the king. Attack the front piece, and the one behind may fall.
beats.speak: Look for two enemy pieces on one line with the more valuable one in front, especially the king. Attack the front piece, and the one behind may fall.

beats.label: Your turn
beats.say: Now try it yourself against the computer. Black's king on e6 and queen on g8 stand on the same diagonal. Find the skewer and win the queen.
beats.speak: Now try it yourself against the computer. Black's king on E six and queen on G eight stand on the same diagonal. Find the skewer and win the queen.

practice.goal: Skewer Black's king and queen with a check, win the queen, and play on to win.

checkpoints.label: Skewer the king and win the queen

hints: Give check along the diagonal that runs through Black's king to the queen behind it. When the king steps aside, the queen can be taken.
Your bishop on f1 can reach that diagonal. Find the square where it checks the king and cannot be taken.
practice.offTrack: That does not win the queen. Undo it: check the king along its diagonal with the queen behind it, then take the queen when the king steps aside.

mistakes.d2d5: Your queen gives check on the right diagonal, but taking Black's queen with her is only an even trade. Undo it and skewer with a cheaper piece.

practice.success: The check forced Black's king off the diagonal, and your bishop took the queen behind it. Even if Black takes your bishop back, you have won a queen for a bishop. Play on.

lessons.title: Discovered Attacks
teaches: Moving one piece can unveil an attack by another piece standing behind it: a discovered attack.
The strongest discovered attacks make two threats at once: one from the piece that moves and one from the piece behind it.
When the uncovered attack is a check, the opponent must answer it first, so the other threat usually succeeds.
In a double check two pieces give check at once, and only a king move can answer it.
Look for your rook, bishop or queen lined up behind one of your own pieces, and watch for the same trick against you.

beats.label: A hidden attacker
beats.say: Sometimes the piece that moves is not the piece that attacks. When it steps aside, it uncovers an attack by a piece standing behind it. This is a discovered attack.
beats.speak: Sometimes the piece that moves is not the piece that attacks. When it steps aside, it uncovers an attack by a piece standing behind it. This is a discovered attack.

beats.label: Front piece, back piece
beats.say: White's rook on d1 points up the d-file towards Black's queen on d7. But White's own bishop on d3 stands in between, so for now the rook's attack is blocked.
beats.speak: White's rook on D one points up the d-file towards Black's queen on D seven. But White's own bishop on D three stands in between, so for now the rook's attack is blocked.

beats.label: Uncovering the rook
beats.say: The bishop steps from d3 to e2. Now nothing stands between the rook and the queen: the rook's attack has been uncovered.
beats.speak: The bishop steps from D three to E two. Now nothing stands between the rook and the queen: the rook's attack has been uncovered.

beats.label: One threat is not enough
beats.say: A single threat like this is easy to meet: Black's queen can simply step to safety. To win something, the piece that moves should make a threat of its own.
beats.speak: A single threat like this is easy to meet: Black's queen can simply step to safety. To win something, the piece that moves should make a threat of its own.

beats.label: Two threats at once
beats.say: Back to the start. This time the bishop takes the pawn on h7 and gives check to Black's king. At the same moment, the rook's attack on the queen is uncovered.
beats.speak: Back to the start. This time the bishop takes the pawn on H seven and gives check to Black's king. At the same moment, the rook's attack on the queen is uncovered.

beats.label: Check first, queen lost
beats.say: Black must answer the check first. Black's king takes the bishop on h7. Then White's rook takes the queen on d7.
beats.speak: Black must answer the check first. Black's king takes the bishop on H seven. Then White's rook takes the queen on D seven.

beats.label: Counting the gain
beats.say: White gave a bishop, worth three, and won the queen, worth nine. The check meant Black had no time to save the queen.
beats.speak: White gave a bishop, worth three, and won the queen, worth nine. The check meant Black had no time to save the queen.

beats.label: A knight unveils a bishop
beats.say: Here White's bishop on b2 aims along the long diagonal towards Black's rook on h8. White's own knight on d4 is in the way.
beats.speak: Here White's bishop on B two aims along the long diagonal towards Black's rook on H eight. White's own knight on D four is in the way.

beats.label: The knight jumps
beats.say: The knight jumps from d4 to b5 and attacks Black's queen on c7. The same jump uncovers the bishop's attack on the rook.
beats.speak: The knight jumps from D four to B five and attacks Black's queen on C seven. The same jump uncovers the bishop's attack on the rook.

beats.label: Black can't save both
beats.say: Black has one move and two pieces under attack. If the queen escapes, the bishop takes the rook, so White wins material either way.
beats.speak: Black has one move and two pieces under attack. If the queen escapes, the bishop takes the rook, so White wins material either way.

beats.label: Discovered check
beats.say: The most dangerous discovered attack uncovers a check. White's rook on e1 aims at Black's king on e8, with White's knight on e5 in between.
beats.speak: The most dangerous discovered attack uncovers a check. White's rook on E one aims at Black's king on E eight, with White's knight on E five in between.

beats.label: The knight attacks the queen
beats.say: The knight jumps from e5 to c4 and attacks the queen on b6. Its jump uncovers the rook's check on Black's king.
beats.speak: The knight jumps from E five to C four and attacks the queen on B six. Its jump uncovers the rook's check on Black's king.

beats.label: No time to save the queen
beats.say: Black has to answer the check, and every answer still loses the queen. Black's king steps to f8. White's knight takes the queen on b6.
beats.speak: Black has to answer the check, and every answer still loses the queen. Black's king steps to F eight. White's knight takes the queen on B six.

beats.label: Double check
beats.say: Here the knight jumps from e4 to d6 and gives check itself, while it also uncovers the rook's check. Two pieces check the king at once: a double check.
beats.speak: Here the knight jumps from E four to D six and gives check itself, while it also uncovers the rook's check. Two pieces check the king at once: a double check.

beats.label: Only the king can move
beats.say: Black cannot block two lines or capture two pieces in one move. Against a double check, only a king move helps. The knight on d6 also attacks Black's queen on b5.
beats.speak: Black cannot block two lines or capture two pieces in one move. Against a double check, only a king move helps. The knight on D six also attacks Black's queen on B five.

beats.label: The queen falls
beats.say: Black's king steps to d8. White's knight takes the queen on b5.
beats.speak: Black's king steps to D eight. White's knight takes the queen on B five.

beats.label: Spot the line-up
beats.say: To find these chances, look for your rook, bishop or queen lined up behind one of your own pieces, pointing at an enemy king or a valuable piece.
beats.speak: To find these chances, look for your rook, bishop or queen lined up behind one of your own pieces, pointing at an enemy king or a valuable piece.

beats.label: Watch out for it too
beats.say: The same trick can be played against you. When an enemy piece stands in front of their own rook, bishop or queen, ask what it would uncover if it moved.
beats.speak: The same trick can be played against you. When an enemy piece stands in front of their own rook, bishop or queen, ask what it would uncover if it moved.

beats.label: Your turn
beats.say: Now you can try it yourself. White's knight on e5 stands between White's rook and Black's king. Find a knight move that uncovers check and wins something.
beats.speak: Now you can try it yourself. White's knight on E five stands between White's rook and Black's king. Find a knight move that uncovers check and wins something.

practice.goal: Move the knight off the e-file to uncover a check from your rook, and win material.
hints: When your knight leaves the e-file, your rook on e1 gives check. Choose a knight move that also attacks something valuable, so Black cannot deal with both.
Black's queen on c5 and rook on h8 are the targets. Which knight jump attacks one of them while your rook gives check?
practice.offTrack: That does not win material. Undo it: uncover the rook's check with a knight move that also attacks something, then capture what Black cannot save.

mistakes.e5d7: The knight on d7 uncovers check and attacks the queen, but Black's king simply takes it. Undo it and find a square the king cannot reach.
mistakes.e5f7: Taking the pawn on f7 uncovers check, but Black's king takes your knight. Undo it and find a knight move the king cannot answer by taking the knight.

practice.success: Your knight uncovered a check from the rook, and Black had to answer it first, so it could not save everything. You won material. Play on.

lessons.title: Removing the Defender
teaches: A guarded piece is hard to win, but it becomes easy once its guard is gone.
One way to remove a defender is to capture it.
Another way is to chase it away, often with a pawn, so it can no longer guard the target.
Before capturing a guard, count what you give and what you win in the whole sequence.
When a target is guarded, ask: can I capture the guard, or chase it away?

beats.label: Taking away a guard
beats.say: A guarded piece is hard to win. But if you remove the piece that guards it, the target is left alone. This idea is called removing the defender.
beats.speak: A guarded piece is hard to win. But if you remove the piece that guards it, the target is left alone. This idea is called removing the defender.

beats.label: The target and its guard
beats.say: White's rook on e1 attacks Black's bishop on e5. Black's knight on c6 guards that bishop.
beats.speak: White's rook on E one attacks Black's bishop on E five. Black's knight on C six guards that bishop.

beats.label: Don't grab too soon
beats.say: If the rook took the bishop now, the knight would take the rook. White would give a rook, worth five, for a bishop, worth three.
beats.speak: If the rook took the bishop now, the knight would take the rook. White would give a rook, worth five, for a bishop, worth three.

beats.label: Capture the guard
beats.say: Instead, White's bishop takes the knight on c6. Black's pawn on b7 takes the bishop back.
beats.speak: Instead, White's bishop takes the knight on C six. Black's pawn on B seven takes the bishop back.

beats.label: The bishop is alone
beats.say: Look at e5 now. The pawn on c6 guards b5 and d5, not e5, so nothing defends Black's bishop any more.
beats.speak: Look at E five now. The pawn on C six guards B five and D five, not E five, so nothing defends Black's bishop any more.

beats.label: Winning the bishop
beats.say: White's rook takes the bishop on e5, and no black piece can take it back.
beats.speak: White's rook takes the bishop on E five, and no black piece can take it back.

beats.label: Adding it up
beats.say: White traded a bishop for a knight, which is an even trade, and then won a whole bishop for free.
beats.speak: White traded a bishop for a knight, which is an even trade, and then won a whole bishop for free.

beats.label: Chasing the guard
beats.say: The second way is to chase the guard away. White's rook on d1 attacks Black's bishop on d5, and Black's knight on f6 guards it.
beats.speak: The second way is to chase the guard away. White's rook on D one attacks Black's bishop on D five, and Black's knight on F six guards it.

beats.label: A pawn attacks the knight
beats.say: White pushes the pawn from e4 to e5, where it threatens to capture the knight on f6.
beats.speak: White pushes the pawn from E four to E five, where it threatens to capture the knight on F six.

beats.label: Black can't keep both
beats.say: If the knight moves away, the bishop loses its guard. If the bishop moves instead, the pawn takes the knight. Black can't save both.
beats.speak: If the knight moves away, the bishop loses its guard. If the bishop moves instead, the pawn takes the knight. Black can't save both.

beats.label: The guard runs away
beats.say: Black's knight runs to d7. White's rook takes the bishop on d5, and it is safe there.
beats.speak: Black's knight runs to D seven. White's rook takes the bishop on D five, and it is safe there.

beats.label: Pawns make good chasers
beats.say: Pawns make excellent chasers. A pawn is worth only one, so a knight or bishop it attacks usually has to run rather than be traded for it.
beats.speak: Pawns make excellent chasers. A pawn is worth only one, so a knight or bishop it attacks usually has to run rather than be traded for it.

beats.label: Count before you capture
beats.say: Before you take a guard, count what you give and what you get. Removing the defender pays off when the whole sequence wins more than it costs.
beats.speak: Before you take a guard, count what you give and what you get. Removing the defender pays off when the whole sequence wins more than it costs.

beats.label: The question to ask
beats.say: So when a piece you want is guarded, ask two questions. Can I capture the guard? Can I chase it away?
beats.speak: So when a piece you want is guarded, ask two questions. Can I capture the guard? Can I chase it away?

beats.label: Your turn
beats.say: Now you can try it yourself. Black's bishop on d4 is attacked by your rook and guarded by the knight on c6. Remove that guard and win the bishop.
beats.speak: Now you can try it yourself. Black's bishop on D four is attacked by your rook and guarded by the knight on C six. Remove that guard and win the bishop.

practice.goal: Remove the knight that guards Black's bishop on d4, then win the bishop.

checkpoints.label: Remove the guard and win the bishop

hints: A guarded piece is hard to win. Count its guards: if you capture or chase away the only one, the piece is left alone.
Which of your pieces attacks the knight on c6, the only guard of Black's bishop?
practice.offTrack: That does not win the bishop. Undo it: first take away the knight that guards it, then capture the bishop with your rook.

mistakes.d1d4: If your rook takes the bishop now, the knight on c6 takes your rook: a rook, worth five, for a bishop, worth three. Undo it and remove the guard first.

practice.success: You traded your bishop for the knight that guarded Black's bishop, and then your rook took the unguarded bishop: a whole bishop won. Play on.

lessons.title: Two-Rook Checkmate
teaches: Two rooks can checkmate a lone king without help from their own king.
One rook guards a rank like a wall while the other gives check on the next rank, then they swap jobs.
Each check pushes the king one rank closer to the edge, like climbing a ladder.
Keep the rooks out of the king's reach: if the king comes close, slide that rook to the far side first.
The ladder works towards any edge of the board.

beats.label: Two rooks, one king
beats.say: Two rooks can checkmate a lone king without any help from their own king. They push the king to the edge one rank at a time, like climbing a ladder.
beats.speak: Two rooks can checkmate a lone king without any help from their own king. They push the king to the edge one rank at a time, like climbing a ladder.

beats.label: The first wall
beats.say: White's rook on a4 guards the whole fourth rank. Black's king on e5 cannot step down onto it.
beats.speak: White's rook on A four guards the whole fourth rank. Black's king on E five cannot step down onto it.

beats.label: Check from the other rook
beats.say: The other rook moves from b3 to b5 and gives check along the fifth rank.
beats.speak: The other rook moves from B three to B five and gives check along the fifth rank.

beats.label: Only one way out
beats.say: Black's king can't stay on the fifth rank, and the fourth rank is guarded. It has to climb to the sixth rank.
beats.speak: Black's king can't stay on the fifth rank, and the fourth rank is guarded. It has to climb to the sixth rank.

beats.label: The rooks swap jobs
beats.say: Black's king steps to f6. The rook from a4 climbs past its partner to a6 and gives check on the sixth rank.
beats.speak: Black's king steps to F six. The rook from A four climbs past its partner to A six and gives check on the sixth rank.

beats.label: Another rung
beats.say: Black's king climbs to g7. The rook on b5 climbs to b7 and gives check on the seventh rank.
beats.speak: Black's king climbs to G seven. The rook on B five climbs to B seven and gives check on the seventh rank.

beats.label: Checkmate
beats.say: Black's king is pushed to g8, on the edge. The rook on a6 goes to a8 and gives check along the last rank. Checkmate!
beats.speak: Black's king is pushed to G eight, on the edge. The rook on A six goes to A eight and gives check along the last rank. Checkmate!

beats.label: Why it's mate
beats.say: The rook on a8 checks the king and guards f8 and h8. The rook on b7 guards every square on the seventh rank. Black's king has nowhere to go.
beats.speak: The rook on A eight checks the king and guards F eight and H eight. The rook on B seven guards every square on the seventh rank. Black's king has nowhere to go.

beats.label: The rooks take turns
beats.say: Notice the pattern: one rook holds a wall while the other checks on the next rank, then they swap jobs. White's king never had to move.
beats.speak: Notice the pattern: one rook holds a wall while the other checks on the next rank, then they swap jobs. White's king never had to move.

beats.label: When the king comes close
beats.say: Now a new position. The rook on a5 holds the fifth rank, so the next step would be the rook from b4 to b6, but b6 is right next to Black's king, which would simply take the rook.
beats.speak: Now a new position. The rook on A five holds the fifth rank, so the next step would be the rook from B four to B six, but B six is right next to Black's king, which would simply take the rook.

beats.label: Slide to the far side
beats.say: So White's rook slides from b4 to h4, far away from the king. Black's king steps to d6.
beats.speak: So White's rook slides from B four to H four, far away from the king. Black's king steps to D six.

beats.label: Check from a distance
beats.say: The rook moves from h4 to h6 and gives check from a safe distance. Black's king climbs to d7.
beats.speak: The rook moves from H four to H six and gives check from a safe distance. Black's king climbs to D seven.

beats.label: Up to the edge
beats.say: The rook on a5 checks from a7. Black's king is pushed to e8, on the edge.
beats.speak: The rook on A five checks from A seven. Black's king is pushed to E eight, on the edge.

beats.label: Mate again
beats.say: The rook on h6 goes to h8: checkmate. Both rooks stayed out of the king's reach the whole time.
beats.speak: The rook on H six goes to H eight: checkmate. Both rooks stayed out of the king's reach the whole time.

beats.label: Any edge works
beats.say: The ladder works towards any edge. The rooks can guard files instead of ranks and drive the king to one side of the board.
beats.speak: The ladder works towards any edge. The rooks can guard files instead of ranks and drive the king to one side of the board.

beats.label: Remember
beats.say: Check with one rook while the other holds the wall. If the king comes close to a rook, slide that rook to the far side first.
beats.speak: Check with one rook while the other holds the wall. If the king comes close to a rook, slide that rook to the far side first.

beats.label: Your turn
beats.say: Now you can try it yourself. Use the rook ladder to drive Black's king to an edge, then checkmate it.
beats.speak: Now you can try it yourself. Use the rook ladder to drive Black's king to an edge, then checkmate it.

practice.goal: Use your two rooks like a ladder to checkmate Black's king.
hints: Climb the ladder: one rook guards a rank as a wall while the other checks on the next rank. If the king comes close to a rook, slide that rook to the far side first.
Black's king is on e4. Put one rook on the third rank as a wall, then check from the fourth rank with the other.
practice.success: Checkmate! Your rooks took turns, one holding a wall while the other gave check, until Black's king had nowhere to go.

lessons.title: Queen Checkmate
teaches: A queen and king can always force checkmate against a lone king, as long as you avoid stalemate.
Build a box: the queen's lines fence the king in, and staying a knight's move away keeps her from giving needless checks.
Shrink the box by following the king, until it is stuck on the edge.
Never take away the king's last square without check: that is stalemate, a draw.
Bring your own king close, then mate with the queen guarded by the king.

beats.label: Queen and king
beats.say: A queen and king against a lone king is an easy win, once you know the method. The queen herds the king to the edge, then White's king helps to finish.
beats.speak: A queen and king against a lone king is an easy win, once you know the method. The queen herds the king to the edge, then White's king helps to finish.

beats.label: Checks are not enough
beats.say: Giving check again and again rarely works, because the king just steps away. Instead, the queen builds a box around the king and makes it smaller.
beats.speak: Giving check again and again rarely works, because the king just steps away. Instead, the queen builds a box around the king and makes it smaller.

beats.label: Building the box
beats.say: White's queen moves from a3 to d3. Now Black's king cannot cross the d-file or the third rank.
beats.speak: White's queen moves from A three to D three. Now Black's king cannot cross the d-file or the third rank.

beats.label: A knight's move away
beats.say: The queen stands a knight's move away from the king. From there she fences the king in without giving check.
beats.speak: The queen stands a knight's move away from the king. From there she fences the king in without giving check.

beats.label: Follow the king
beats.say: Black's king steps to f6. The queen follows to e4, again a knight's move away, and the box is smaller.
beats.speak: Black's king steps to F six. The queen follows to E four, again a knight's move away, and the box is smaller.

beats.label: Smaller again
beats.say: Black's king goes to g7. The queen follows to f5, and the box shrinks again.
beats.speak: Black's king goes to G seven. The queen follows to F five, and the box shrinks again.

beats.label: Trapped on the edge
beats.say: Black's king tries h6. The queen steps to g4, and now the king is trapped on h6, h7 and h8.
beats.speak: Black's king tries H six. The queen steps to G four, and now the king is trapped on H six, H seven and H eight.

beats.label: Two squares left
beats.say: Black's king goes to h7. The queen moves up to g5. Only h7 and h8 are left for the king.
beats.speak: Black's king goes to H seven. The queen moves up to G five. Only H seven and H eight are left for the king.

beats.label: Stop squeezing
beats.say: Black's king goes to h8. The box can't get any smaller, so the queen's work is done. Now it is time to bring White's king.
beats.speak: Black's king goes to H eight. The box can't get any smaller, so the queen's work is done. Now it is time to bring White's king.

beats.label: The stalemate trap
beats.say: Watch what happens if the queen squeezes anyway and goes to g6. Black's king is not in check, but g8, g7 and h7 are all guarded. Black has no legal move: stalemate, a draw.
beats.speak: Watch what happens if the queen squeezes anyway and goes to G six. Black's king is not in check, but G eight, G seven and H seven are all guarded. Black has no legal move: stalemate, a draw.

beats.label: Leave the king a square
beats.say: So the queen stays on g5 and leaves Black's king the square h7. Never take away the last square unless it is checkmate.
beats.speak: So the queen stays on G five and leaves Black's king the square H seven. Never take away the last square unless it is checkmate.

beats.label: The king walks up
beats.say: White's king steps to f3. Black's king goes to h7. White's king steps to f4. Black's king goes back to h8.
beats.speak: White's king steps to F three. Black's king goes to H seven. White's king steps to F four. Black's king goes back to H eight.

beats.label: Closer still
beats.say: White's king steps to f5. Black's king goes to h7. White's king steps to f6. Black's king returns to h8.
beats.speak: White's king steps to F five. Black's king goes to H seven. White's king steps to F six. Black's king returns to H eight.

beats.label: Checkmate
beats.say: Now the queen goes to g7 and gives check. White's king on f6 guards her, so Black's king cannot take her. Checkmate!
beats.speak: Now the queen goes to G seven and gives check. White's king on F six guards her, so Black's king cannot take her. Checkmate!

beats.label: Why it's mate
beats.say: The queen on g7 also guards g8 and h7, the king's only other squares. There is no escape and no capture, so the king is mated.
beats.speak: The queen on G seven also guards G eight and H seven, the king's only other squares. There is no escape and no capture, so the king is mated.

beats.label: The method
beats.say: Remember the four steps: build the box, shrink it, stop before stalemate, then bring your king and mate.
beats.speak: Remember the four steps: build the box, shrink it, stop before stalemate, then bring your king and mate.

beats.label: Check for stalemate
beats.say: Before each queen move near the edge, ask: will Black's king still have a move? If it would have none and is not in check, choose a different move.
beats.speak: Before each queen move near the edge, ask: will Black's king still have a move? If it would have none and is not in check, choose a different move.

beats.label: Your turn
beats.say: Now you can try it yourself. Box in Black's king with your queen, bring your own king up, and checkmate.
beats.speak: Now you can try it yourself. Box in Black's king with your queen, bring your own king up, and checkmate.

practice.goal: Checkmate Black's king with your queen and king, without allowing stalemate.
hints: Build a box: keep your queen a knight's move from Black's king and follow it, making the box smaller. Stop before stalemate and bring your king up to help.
Your king on c1 must walk up the board to guard the queen's final square. Before each queen move near the edge, check that Black's king can still move.
practice.success: Checkmate! Your queen boxed in Black's king, your king came up to guard her, and you never took away the king's last square too early.

lessons.title: Rook Checkmate
teaches: With its own king helping, a single rook is enough to force mate against a bare king.
The rook builds a box by guarding a rank or file the enemy king cannot cross.
Walk your king up; when the kings face each other with one square between, the rook checks and the box shrinks.
On the edge, mate comes when the kings face each other and the rook checks along the edge.
Near the corner, never take away the king's last square without check: that is stalemate.

beats.label: Rook and king
beats.say: One rook plus its king is also enough to mate a bare king. It takes longer than with a queen, and the rook needs its king's help all the way.
beats.speak: One rook plus its king is also enough to mate a bare king. It takes longer than with a queen, and the rook needs its king's help all the way.

beats.label: Building the box
beats.say: White's rook on h4 guards the whole fourth rank. Black's king is boxed into the top half of the board, ranks 5 to 8.
beats.speak: White's rook on H four guards the whole fourth rank. Black's king is boxed into the top half of the board, ranks 5 to 8.

beats.label: The king comes up
beats.say: A rook alone can't finish the job, so White's king walks up to help. White's king steps to d3. Black's king steps forward to d5.
beats.speak: A rook alone can't finish the job, so White's king walks up to help. White's king steps to D three. Black's king steps forward to D five.

beats.label: Kings face to face
beats.say: The kings now face each other with one square between them. White's king guards c4, d4 and e4, so a rook check now will push Black's king back.
beats.speak: The kings now face each other with one square between them. White's king guards C four, D four and E four, so a rook check now will push Black's king back.

beats.label: Check and shrink
beats.say: The rook moves up to h5 and gives check. Black's king cannot go down, so it retreats to c6. The box is now ranks 6 to 8.
beats.speak: The rook moves up to H five and gives check. Black's king cannot go down, so it retreats to C six. The box is now ranks 6 to 8.

beats.label: Repeat the steps
beats.say: White repeats these steps. The king walks up, and whenever the kings face each other, the rook checks and the box shrinks by one rank.
beats.speak: White repeats these steps. The king walks up, and whenever the kings face each other, the rook checks and the box shrinks by one rank.

beats.label: Near the edge
beats.say: A few moves later, the rook guards the sixth rank and the kings face each other again, with White to move.
beats.speak: A few moves later, the rook guards the sixth rank and the kings face each other again, with White to move.

beats.label: Pushed to the edge
beats.say: The rook checks from h7. Black's king is pushed to c8, on the edge.
beats.speak: The rook checks from H seven. Black's king is pushed to C eight, on the edge.

beats.label: The king follows
beats.say: White's king follows to d6. Black's king steps to b8, keeping away from the white king.
beats.speak: White's king follows to D six. Black's king steps to B eight, keeping away from the white king.

beats.label: Facing means mate
beats.say: If Black's king had gone to d8 instead, facing White's king, the rook would have given mate at once from h8.
beats.speak: If Black's king had gone to D eight instead, facing White's king, the rook would have given mate at once from H eight.

beats.label: Into the corner
beats.say: White's king follows again, to c6. Black's king runs into the corner, to a8.
beats.speak: White's king follows again, to C six. Black's king runs into the corner, to A eight.

beats.label: The stalemate trap
beats.say: Careful here! Suppose the rook went to b7. It is guarded by White's king, a7 and b8 are covered, and Black's king is not in check. Black has no legal move: stalemate, a draw.
beats.speak: Careful here! Suppose the rook went to B seven. It is guarded by White's king, A seven and B eight are covered, and Black's king is not in check. Black has no legal move: stalemate, a draw.

beats.label: The right way
beats.say: Instead, White's king steps to b6. Black's king must go to b8, its only square.
beats.speak: Instead, White's king steps to B six. Black's king must go to B eight, its only square.

beats.label: Checkmate
beats.say: Now the kings face each other, and the rook checks from h8. White's king covers a7, b7 and c7, and the rook covers the last rank. Checkmate!
beats.speak: Now the kings face each other, and the rook checks from H eight. White's king covers A seven, B seven and C seven, and the rook covers the last rank. Checkmate!

beats.label: The method
beats.say: Remember the method: box the king in with the rook, walk your king up, and check when the kings face each other. Each check makes the box smaller.
beats.speak: Remember the method: box the king in with the rook, walk your king up, and check when the kings face each other. Each check makes the box smaller.

beats.label: Watch for stalemate
beats.say: Near the corner, always make sure Black's king still has a move. A rook move that takes away its last square without check throws the win away.
beats.speak: Near the corner, always make sure Black's king still has a move. A rook move that takes away its last square without check throws the win away.

beats.label: Your turn
beats.say: Now you can try it yourself. Box in Black's king with your rook, bring up your king, and checkmate.
beats.speak: Now you can try it yourself. Box in Black's king with your rook, bring up your king, and checkmate.

practice.goal: Checkmate Black's king with your rook and king, without allowing stalemate.
hints: Box the king in with your rook, walk your own king up, and give check with the rook when the two kings face each other.
Your rook on h1 can guard a whole rank or file to start the box. Then bring your king from e1 towards Black's king.
practice.success: Checkmate! Your rook made the box smaller with each check, and your king guarded the squares the rook could not.

lessons.title: Winning Material Puzzles
teaches: Winning material means capturing more points than you give back.
Before capturing, count who attacks and who defends the target.
An undefended piece can often be taken for free.
A fork attacks two targets at once, so your opponent often can save only one.
A piece pinned to its king cannot move away, so attack it again, ideally with a pawn.

beats.label: Solving together
beats.say: In this lesson we solve four short puzzles together. In each one, White is to move and can win material.
beats.speak: In this lesson we solve four short puzzles together. In each one, White is to move and can win material.

beats.label: Three questions
beats.say: Before every move, ask three questions. What can I capture safely? Can one move attack two things? Is any piece stuck and unable to move?
beats.speak: Before every move, ask three questions. What can I capture safely? Can one move attack two things? Is any piece stuck and unable to move?

beats.label: Puzzle one
beats.say: Puzzle one. White to move. Look for a black piece you can take without losing anything in return.
beats.speak: Puzzle one. White to move. Look for a black piece you can take without losing anything in return.

beats.label: Two guarded pawns
beats.say: The bishop on d3 can reach the pawns on b5 and h7, but both are guarded. The pawn on a6 guards b5, and the king guards h7.
beats.speak: The bishop on D three can reach the pawns on B five and H seven, but both are guarded. The pawn on A six guards B five, and the king guards H seven.

beats.label: An unguarded knight
beats.say: Now look at the knight on e6. The rook on e1 attacks it, and no black piece or pawn guards it.
beats.speak: Now look at the knight on E six. The rook on E one attacks it, and no black piece or pawn guards it.

beats.label: A free knight
beats.say: White's rook captures the knight on e6. Nothing can take the rook back, so White wins three points for free.
beats.speak: White's rook captures the knight on E six. Nothing can take the rook back, so White wins three points for free.

beats.label: Puzzle two
beats.say: Puzzle two. Black's knight on f6 attacks White's knight on d5. Before you retreat, look for a jump that attacks two things.
beats.speak: Puzzle two. Black's knight on F six attacks White's knight on D five. Before you retreat, look for a jump that attacks two things.

beats.label: The knight fork
beats.say: White's knight jumps from d5 to c7. It checks the king on e8 and attacks the rook on a8 at the same time. That is a fork.
beats.speak: White's knight jumps from D five to C seven. It checks the king on E eight and attacks the rook on A eight at the same time. That is a fork.

beats.label: The king must move
beats.say: Black must get out of check first, so the king steps from e8 to e7. The rook is left behind.
beats.speak: Black must get out of check first, so the king steps from E eight to E seven. The rook is left behind.

beats.label: Collecting the rook
beats.say: White's knight captures the rook on a8. White has won five points.
beats.speak: White's knight captures the rook on A eight. White has won five points.

beats.label: Puzzle three
beats.say: Puzzle three. Black's bishop on b4 has no defender. Can White's queen attack it and the king together?
beats.speak: Puzzle three. Black's bishop on B four has no defender. Can White's queen attack it and the king together?

beats.label: The queen fork
beats.say: White's queen moves from d1 to a4. She checks the king along the diagonal and attacks the bishop along the rank.
beats.speak: White's queen moves from D one to A four. She checks the king along the diagonal and attacks the bishop along the rank.

beats.label: Blocking the check
beats.say: Black blocks the check by moving the pawn from c7 to c6. That stops the check, but it does not guard the bishop.
beats.speak: Black blocks the check by moving the pawn from C seven to C six. That stops the check, but it does not guard the bishop.

beats.label: Taking the bishop
beats.say: White's queen captures the bishop on b4, and nothing can take her back. White has won three points.
beats.speak: White's queen captures the bishop on B four, and nothing can take her back. White has won three points.

beats.label: Puzzle four
beats.say: Puzzle four. The bishop on b5 aims along the diagonal at the black king on e8. Only the knight on c6 stands in between.
beats.speak: Puzzle four. The bishop on B five aims along the diagonal at the black king on E eight. Only the knight on C six stands in between.

beats.label: A pinned knight
beats.say: The knight is pinned. If it moved, the king would be in check, and that is not allowed. How can White attack the knight again?
beats.speak: The knight is pinned. If it moved, the king would be in check, and that is not allowed. How can White attack the knight again?

beats.label: The pawn attacks
beats.say: White's pawn moves from d4 to d5 and attacks the pinned knight. The knight cannot run away.
beats.speak: White's pawn moves from D four to D five and attacks the pinned knight. The knight cannot run away.

beats.label: Too late to escape
beats.say: Black's king steps from e8 to f8 to end the pin. But that used Black's turn, and the knight is still attacked.
beats.speak: Black's king steps from E eight to F eight to end the pin. But that used Black's turn, and the knight is still attacked.

beats.label: Pawn takes knight
beats.say: White's pawn captures the knight on c6. Even if the pawn on b7 takes back, White has swapped a one-point pawn for a three-point knight.
beats.speak: White's pawn captures the knight on C six. Even if the pawn on B seven takes back, White has swapped a one-point pawn for a three-point knight.

beats.label: What we used
beats.say: We found a free piece, a knight fork, a queen fork and a pin. Each time, White won more points than it gave.
beats.speak: We found a free piece, a knight fork, a queen fork and a pin. Each time, White won more points than it gave.

beats.label: Your turn
beats.say: In your own games, ask the three questions before every move, for your pieces as well as your opponent's.
beats.speak: In your own games, ask the three questions before every move, for your pieces as well as your opponent's.

lessons.title: Mate in One Puzzles
teaches: A mate in one is a single move that checkmates.
For each check, ask: can the king move, can the check be blocked, can the checker be captured?
A king stuck behind its own pawns can be mated on the back rank.
A queen right beside the king, guarded by her own king, often gives mate.
Moving one piece can uncover a check from another, and that can be mate.

beats.label: One move to win
beats.say: A mate in one is a single move that checkmates. In this lesson we look at three patterns that appear again and again.
beats.speak: A mate in one is a single move that checkmates. In this lesson we look at three patterns that appear again and again.

beats.label: Testing a check
beats.say: For every check you can give, ask three questions. Can the king move? Can the check be blocked? Can the checking piece be captured? Three noes mean checkmate.
beats.speak: For every check you can give, ask three questions. Can the king move? Can the check be blocked? Can the checking piece be captured? Three noes mean checkmate.

beats.label: The back rank
beats.say: Pattern one: the back rank. Black's king on g8 sits behind its own pawns on f7, g7 and h7. White to move.
beats.speak: Pattern one: the back rank. Black's king on G eight sits behind its own pawns on F seven, G seven and H seven. White to move.

beats.label: Rook to the back rank
beats.say: White's rook moves from e1 to e8 and checks the king along the back rank.
beats.speak: White's rook moves from E one to E eight and checks the king along the back rank.

beats.label: No way out
beats.say: The pawns block the squares in front of the king, and the rook covers f8 and h8. Nothing can block or capture the rook. Checkmate.
beats.speak: The pawns block the squares in front of the king, and the rook covers F eight and H eight. Nothing can block or capture the rook. Checkmate.

beats.label: An escape square
beats.say: Now Black's pawn stands on h6 instead of h7. White's rook moves from e1 to e8 again, but this time h7 is empty.
beats.speak: Now Black's pawn stands on H six instead of H seven. White's rook moves from E one to E eight again, but this time H seven is empty.

beats.label: The king slips away
beats.say: Black's king steps from g8 to h7, so it is only check. One small pawn move gave the king room to breathe.
beats.speak: Black's king steps from G eight to H seven, so it is only check. One small pawn move gave the king room to breathe.

beats.label: Queen and king
beats.say: Pattern two: queen and king together. Black's king is in the corner on h8, and White's king on g6 stands close by.
beats.speak: Pattern two: queen and king together. Black's king is in the corner on H eight, and White's king on G six stands close by.

beats.label: Queen beside the king
beats.say: White's queen moves from a7 to g7, right beside the black king. White's king on g6 guards her.
beats.speak: White's queen moves from A seven to G seven, right beside the black king. White's king on G six guards her.

beats.label: Why it is mate
beats.say: The king cannot take the guarded queen, and she covers g8 and h7 as well. Checkmate.
beats.speak: The king cannot take the guarded queen, and she covers G eight and H seven as well. Checkmate.

beats.label: Careful: stalemate
beats.say: Now watch the queen go from a7 to f7 instead. The king is not in check, yet g8, g7 and h7 are all covered.
beats.speak: Now watch the queen go from A seven to F seven instead. The king is not in check, yet G eight, G seven and H seven are all covered.

beats.label: Saved by a pawn
beats.say: Only Black's pawn on b5 can still move. Without it, Black would have no legal move and no check: stalemate, a draw. When you trap a king, make sure you give check or leave Black a move.
beats.speak: Only Black's pawn on B five can still move. Without it, Black would have no legal move and no check: stalemate, a draw. When you trap a king, make sure you give check or leave Black a move.

beats.label: A discovered mate
beats.say: Pattern three: a discovered mate. White's rook on e1 aims at the king on e8, but White's own knight on e7 is in the way.
beats.speak: Pattern three: a discovered mate. White's rook on E one aims at the king on E eight, but White's own knight on E seven is in the way.

beats.label: A boxed-in king
beats.say: Black's own rooks and pawns surround the king on d8, f8, d7 and f7. What happens if the knight moves?
beats.speak: Black's own rooks and pawns surround the king on D eight, F eight, D seven and F seven. What happens if the knight moves?

beats.label: The knight steps aside
beats.say: White's knight jumps from e7 to f5. The rook's line opens, and the king is in check.
beats.speak: White's knight jumps from E seven to F five. The rook's line opens, and the king is in check.

beats.label: Mate from afar
beats.say: The king cannot go to e7, which the rook covers. No black piece can block or take the rook. Checkmate by a rook that never moved.
beats.speak: The king cannot go to E seven, which the rook covers. No black piece can block or take the rook. Checkmate by a rook that never moved.

beats.label: Three patterns
beats.say: Back rank, queen and king, and discovered mate. Watch for them in your games.
beats.speak: Back rank, queen and king, and discovered mate. Watch for them in your games.

beats.label: Guard your own king
beats.say: Before each move, also ask whether your opponent has a mate in one. Spotting it first can save the game.
beats.speak: Before each move, also ask whether your opponent has a mate in one. Spotting it first can save the game.

lessons.title: A Famous Short Game
teaches: Bring out your knights and bishops before going after material.
A king left in the centre can be attacked along open files.
Castling queenside can put a rook on an open file at once.
A sacrifice gives up material on purpose to reach a bigger goal.
In a double check no other piece can answer both checks, so the king must move, sometimes by capturing a checker.
Checkmate ends the game, however many points either side is ahead.

beats.label: Vienna, 1910
beats.say: In Vienna in 1910, Richard Réti played White against Savielly Tartakower. The game lasted only eleven moves and ended with a famous queen sacrifice.
beats.speak: In Vienna in nineteen ten, Richard Ray-tee played White against Savielly Tartakower. The game lasted only eleven moves and ended with a famous queen sacrifice.

beats.label: The starting position
beats.say: Here is the starting position. Watch how quickly a king gets into trouble when it stays in the centre.
beats.speak: Here is the starting position. Watch how quickly a king gets into trouble when it stays in the centre.

beats.label: Move one
beats.say: White opens by pushing a pawn two squares, from e2 to e4. Black answers with the pawn from c7 to c6, getting ready to fight for the centre.
beats.speak: White opens by pushing a pawn two squares, from E two to E four. Black answers with the pawn from C seven to C six, getting ready to fight for the centre.

beats.label: Move two
beats.say: White adds a second centre pawn, from d2 to d4. Black pushes a pawn from d7 to d5, and it attacks the pawn on e4.
beats.speak: White adds a second centre pawn, from D two to D four. Black pushes a pawn from D seven to D five, and it attacks the pawn on E four.

beats.label: Move three
beats.say: White's knight comes out from b1 to c3 to guard e4. Black's pawn captures the pawn on e4 anyway.
beats.speak: White's knight comes out from B one to C three to guard E four. Black's pawn captures the pawn on E four anyway.

beats.label: Move four
beats.say: White's knight takes back on e4. Black's knight comes out from g8 to f6 and attacks it.
beats.speak: White's knight takes back on E four. Black's knight comes out from G eight to F six and attacks it.

beats.label: Move five
beats.say: White's queen steps from d1 to d3 to guard the knight. Black pushes a pawn from e7 to e5, offering it to the pawn on d4.
beats.speak: White's queen steps from D one to D three to guard the knight. Black pushes a pawn from E seven to E five, offering it to the pawn on D four.

beats.label: Move six
beats.say: White's pawn captures on e5. Black's queen moves from d8 to a5 and gives check to the king on e1.
beats.speak: White's pawn captures on E five. Black's queen moves from D eight to A five and gives check to the king on E one.

beats.label: Move seven
beats.say: White's bishop moves from c1 to d2 and blocks the check. Black's queen captures the pawn on e5. Now the knight on e4 is attacked twice.
beats.speak: White's bishop moves from C one to D two and blocks the check. Black's queen captures the pawn on E five. Now the knight on E four is attacked twice.

beats.label: Counting pieces out
beats.say: Compare the two sides. White has a knight, a bishop and the queen in play. Black has only the queen and one knight out, and the black king has not castled.
beats.speak: Compare the two sides. White has a knight, a bishop and the queen in play. Black has only the queen and one knight out, and the black king has not castled.

beats.label: Move eight: castling
beats.say: White castles queenside. First the king slides two squares, from e1 to c1. Then the rook hops over it, from a1 to d1, onto the d-file.
beats.speak: White castles queenside. First the king slides two squares, from E one to C one. Then the rook hops over it, from A one to D one, onto the d-file.

beats.label: A knight left behind
beats.say: By castling, White leaves the knight on e4 to be taken. It looks like a mistake.
beats.speak: By castling, White leaves the knight on E four to be taken. It looks like a mistake.

beats.label: Black grabs the knight
beats.say: Black's knight captures the knight on e4. Black is now a whole piece ahead.
beats.speak: Black's knight captures the knight on E four. Black is now a whole piece ahead.

beats.label: Look at the d-file
beats.say: But look at the black king on e8. The d-file is open all the way to d8, right beside it. Can you find White's shocking move?
beats.speak: But look at the black king on E eight. The d-file is open all the way to D eight, right beside it. Can you find White's shocking move?

beats.label: Move nine: queen sacrifice
beats.say: White's queen moves from d3 to d8 and gives check. This is a sacrifice: the king can simply take her.
beats.speak: White's queen moves from D three to D eight and gives check. This is a sacrifice: the king can simply take her.

beats.label: The king takes
beats.say: Black's king captures the queen on d8. Black is now ahead by a queen and a knight. Was White's sacrifice a mistake?
beats.speak: Black's king captures the queen on D eight. Black is now ahead by a queen and a knight. Was White's sacrifice a mistake?

beats.label: Move ten: double check
beats.say: White's bishop moves from d2 to g5. Now the bishop on g5 and the rook on d1 both check the king. This is a double check.
beats.speak: White's bishop moves from D two to G five. Now the bishop on G five and the rook on D one both check the king. This is a double check.

beats.label: Only the king can move
beats.say: No other black piece can answer both checks at once, so the king must move. Here it cannot capture either checker, and it has only two squares, c7 and e8.
beats.speak: No other black piece can answer both checks at once, so the king must move. Here it cannot capture either checker, and it has only two squares, C seven and E eight.

beats.label: The other way loses too
beats.say: If the king went to e8, the rook would move to d8 and give checkmate. So Black tries the other square.
beats.speak: If the king went to E eight, the rook would move to D eight and give checkmate. So Black tries the other square.

beats.label: King to c7
beats.say: Black's king steps from d8 to c7.
beats.speak: Black's king steps from D eight to C seven.

beats.label: Move eleven: checkmate
beats.say: White's bishop moves from g5 to d8. Checkmate!
beats.speak: White's bishop moves from G five to D eight. Checkmate!

beats.label: Why it is mate
beats.say: The bishop checks the king and covers b6. The rook guards the bishop and covers d6 and d7. Black's own pieces fill the other squares.
beats.speak: The bishop checks the king and covers B six. The rook guards the bishop and covers D six and D seven. Black's own pieces fill the other squares.

beats.label: What we learn
beats.say: White developed pieces and castled, while Black grabbed material and left the king in the centre.
beats.speak: White developed pieces and castled, while Black grabbed material and left the king in the centre.

beats.label: Mate beats material
beats.say: At the end Black was far ahead in points, yet lost. Checkmate ends the game, no matter what is left on the board.
beats.speak: At the end Black was far ahead in points, yet lost. Checkmate ends the game, no matter what is left on the board.

puzzles.title: Introduction · 1

exercise.prompt: Which player makes the first move of a chess game?

puzzles.explanation: White always moves first. After that, the players take turns, one move each.

puzzles.title: Introduction · 2

exercise.prompt: The black king is in check. Select the white piece that attacks it.

puzzles.explanation: The rook attacks straight up the open column to the black king. The knight and the bishop cannot reach the king's square.

puzzles.title: The Chessboard · 1

exercise.prompt: Select the square f6.

puzzles.context: A white knight waits on the square you are looking for.
puzzles.explanation: f6 is where the f-file meets the sixth rank: go along to the f-file, then count up six. The white knight stands there.

puzzles.title: The Chessboard · 2

exercise.prompt: When you sit at the board as White, which corner square is on your right?

puzzles.explanation: The files run from a on White's left to h on White's right, and White's nearest rank is 1, so the right-hand corner is h1. It is a light square.

puzzles.title: The Pawn · 1

exercise.prompt: Choose every square the white pawn on d2 can move to.

puzzles.context: The pawn has not moved yet.
puzzles.explanation: The pawn can step to d3, or make its double step to d4 because both squares are empty. It can also capture diagonally forward: the knight on c3 or the bishop on e3. The rook on f4 is out of its reach.

puzzles.title: The Pawn · 2

exercise.prompt: Choose every black piece that a white pawn attacks.

puzzles.explanation: The pawn on c5 attacks b6 and d6, and the pawn on g4 attacks f5 and h5. The pieces straight ahead on c6 and g5 only block the pawns, and the bishop on f3 is behind the pawn on g4.

puzzles.title: Pawn Duel · 1

exercise.prompt: In Pawn Duel, what happens when a white pawn reaches the eighth rank?
choices: The pawn must stop and wait
The pawn goes back to the second rank

puzzles.explanation: Reaching the far rank wins Pawn Duel at once. Pawns never promote in this game.

puzzles.title: Pawn Duel · 2

exercise.prompt: Choose every black pawn that a white pawn can capture right now.

puzzles.context: A moment from a game of Pawn Duel.
puzzles.explanation: The pawn on c4 can take on b5 or d5, the pawn on e4 can also take on d5, and the pawn on f3 can take on g4. The pawn on e5 is straight in front of a white pawn, so it cannot be captured.

puzzles.title: The Rook · 1

exercise.prompt: Mark every square the white rook on e4 can move to.

puzzles.explanation: The rook moves along the e-file and the fourth rank. Its own pawn on e7 stops it at e6. It can capture the knight on b4 and the pawn on g4, but cannot go past them.

puzzles.title: The Rook · 2

exercise.prompt: White to move. Capture a black piece with the rook without letting Black take the rook back.

puzzles.explanation: The rook slides along the third rank and takes Black's rook on a3, where nothing can capture it back. Taking the pawn on d6 would lose the rook to the pawn on e7.

puzzles.title: Rook Practice · 1

exercise.prompt: Rook Sweep: which black pieces can White's rook capture right now?

puzzles.context: In Rook Sweep only the rooks move; the pawns are targets.
puzzles.explanation: Up the d-file the rook reaches the pawn on d7, and along the fourth rank it reaches the pawn on a4. White's own pawn on f4 shields the pawn on h4.

puzzles.title: Rook Practice · 2

exercise.prompt: In Rook Sweep, which pieces may move?

puzzles.explanation: In Rook Sweep the pawns never move. Each side moves its rook to capture the opposing pawns.

puzzles.title: The Bishop · 1

exercise.prompt: Mark every square the white bishop on f4 can move to.

puzzles.explanation: The bishop moves along its four diagonals. Its own pawn on d6 stops it at e5, and it can capture the rook on h6 and the knight on c1.

puzzles.title: The Bishop · 2

exercise.prompt: White to move. Find the bishop move that safely attacks both black rooks at once.

puzzles.explanation: From d5 the bishop attacks the rook on b7 and the rook on f3, in opposite directions along the same long diagonal. Neither rook can capture the bishop, and Black can move only one of them.

puzzles.title: Bishop Practice · 1

exercise.prompt: Bishop Sweep: which black pieces can White's bishops capture right now?

puzzles.context: In Bishop Sweep only the bishops move; the pawns are targets.
puzzles.explanation: The dark-squared bishop on c3 can take the pawn on b4, which shields the pawn on a5. The light-squared bishop on e2 can take the pawn on g4 through the empty f3 square.

puzzles.title: Bishop Practice · 2

exercise.prompt: In this Bishop Sweep position, White's bishop on d3 and the pawn on f5 stand on light squares, while Black's bishop on f8 and the pawns on a5 and e5 stand on dark squares. What is the result?

puzzles.context: Bishop Sweep, White to move.
puzzles.explanation: Each bishop keeps its square colour. White's light-squared bishop can never reach the black pawns or Black's bishop, which all stand on dark squares, and Black's dark-squared bishop can never reach the white pawn or White's bishop, which stand on light squares. No remaining target can be reached, so the game is a draw.

puzzles.title: The Queen · 1

exercise.prompt: Which squares can the white queen on c4 move to?

puzzles.explanation: Along the c-file she stops before her pawn on c7. On the fourth rank she can capture the bishop on g4, and on the diagonals she can capture the knight on f7 and the pawn on a6. Towards e2 she can go only as far as d3, because her own pawn stands on e2.

puzzles.title: The Queen · 2

exercise.prompt: White to move. Which capture with the queen wins material safely?

puzzles.explanation: The queen captures the rook on a5, and no black piece can reach her there. Taking the knight on d6 would lose her to the pawn on e7.

puzzles.title: Queen Practice · 1

exercise.prompt: Which white pawns are not protected by another pawn?

puzzles.context: Queen Against Pawns. The queen looks for pawns she can take without being captured.
puzzles.explanation: The pawns on a2, c2, g2 and h4 have no pawn guarding them. The pawn on b3 is protected by a2 and c2, f3 by g2, and e4 by f3.

puzzles.title: Queen Practice · 2

exercise.prompt: Which white pawns does the black queen on e5 attack?

puzzles.explanation: The queen attacks e3 down the file, and c3 and f4 along her diagonals. The pawns on b2 and h2 are on those diagonals too, but hidden behind c3 and f4.

puzzles.title: The Knight · 1

exercise.prompt: Which squares can the white knight on d5 move to?

puzzles.explanation: The knight jumps over the pawns beside it. It cannot land on its own pawns on e3 and c7, but it can capture the black pawn on f6.

puzzles.title: The Knight · 2

exercise.prompt: White to move. Find the knight jump that attacks the black queen and rook together.

puzzles.explanation: From c7 the knight attacks both the queen on e8 and the rook on a8. No black piece can capture it there, and Black cannot move both pieces away at once, so White wins material.

puzzles.title: Knight Practice · 1

exercise.prompt: Which black pieces does the white knight on c6 attack?

puzzles.context: Knight Capture. Black's knight has already captured all of White's other pieces.
puzzles.explanation: From c6 the knight can jump to a5, taking the pawn, or to e7, taking the bishop.

puzzles.title: Knight Practice · 2

exercise.prompt: In Knight Corners, which two empty squares does the black pawn on e5 forbid?

puzzles.explanation: Black pawns capture diagonally towards rank 1, so the pawn on e5 covers d4 and f4. The knight may not land on either.

puzzles.title: The King · 1

exercise.prompt: Which squares can the white king move to?

puzzles.explanation: The rook on h1 attacks a1, b1 and c1, and a3, b3 and c3 touch the black king. Only a2 and c2 are safe.

puzzles.title: The King · 2

exercise.prompt: How many points is the king worth?
choices: It has no point value: it is never traded or captured
exercise.answer: It has no point value: it is never traded or captured

puzzles.explanation: The king is beyond value. It is never captured, and if it is checkmated the game is over.

puzzles.title: Safe Squares · 1

exercise.prompt: Walk the white king from a1 to c8, stepping only on safe squares.

puzzles.explanation: The rook's line along the fourth rank stops at the pawn on c4, and the bishop covers b4, so the king crosses at a4. From there b5, c6 and c7 lead safely to c8.

puzzles.title: Safe Squares · 2

exercise.prompt: Which squares can the white king safely move to?

puzzles.explanation: The rook covers c3, d3 and e3, the bishop covers c3 and c5, and the pawn on f5 attacks e4. That leaves c4, d5 and e5.

puzzles.title: Check and Checkmate · 1

exercise.prompt: White to move. Find the checkmate.

puzzles.explanation: The rook checks along the eighth rank. The black king's own pawns block g7 and h7, and the rook covers g8, so there is no escape.

puzzles.title: Check and Checkmate · 2

exercise.prompt: White is in check. Find the only way out.

puzzles.explanation: The king cannot move: f1 and h1 are both on the rook's rank. Nothing can block on f1, but the knight on d3 can capture the rook on e1.

puzzles.title: Setting Up the Board · 1

exercise.prompt: On which square does the white queen start?

puzzles.explanation: White's queen begins on d1. That square is light, matching her colour, and the white king stands next to her on e1.

puzzles.title: Setting Up the Board · 2

exercise.prompt: Select both squares where Black's knights start.

puzzles.explanation: From each corner the order is rook, knight, bishop, so Black's knights start on b8 and g8, right next to the rooks.

puzzles.title: Castling · 1

exercise.prompt: White to move. Castle kingside.

puzzles.explanation: The king moves two squares from e1 to g1, and the rook jumps from h1 to f1.

puzzles.title: Castling · 2

exercise.prompt: After White castles on the queenside, where do the king and rook stand?

puzzles.explanation: The king moves two squares from e1 to c1, and the rook jumps over it from a1 to d1.

puzzles.title: Castling Rules · 1

exercise.prompt: White to move. Castle on the side where it is allowed.

puzzles.explanation: The bishop on b5 attacks f1, so the king cannot cross it to castle kingside. On the queenside d1 and c1 are safe, so White castles there.

puzzles.title: Castling Rules · 2

exercise.prompt: The white king and the a1 rook have never moved, and b1, c1 and d1 are empty. A black bishop attacks b1, but c1, d1 and e1 are safe. May White castle queenside?
choices: Yes: only the rook passes over b1
No: no square between them may be attacked
Only after the bishop is captured
exercise.answer: Yes: only the rook passes over b1

puzzles.explanation: The king must not start, cross or land on an attacked square. It never touches b1, so an attack on b1 does not matter.

puzzles.title: Promotion and En Passant · 1

exercise.prompt: Promote a pawn.

puzzles.explanation: The pawn on e7 steps to e8, where it can become a queen. The pawn on b6 still needs two more moves.

puzzles.title: Promotion and En Passant · 2

exercise.prompt: Black's pawn has just moved from c7 to c5. Find the move that gives check.

puzzles.explanation: The pawn on d5 captures en passant by moving to c6, and the black pawn on c5 is removed. From c6 the pawn attacks the king on b7. This capture is only allowed straight after Black's double step.

puzzles.title: Draws · 1

exercise.prompt: White to move. Give checkmate, and be careful not to stalemate Black.

puzzles.explanation: The queen on d8 or f8 checks the king along the back rank, and the white king covers a7 and b7. Moving the queen to c7 instead would leave Black with no legal move: stalemate.

puzzles.title: Draws · 2

exercise.prompt: It is Black's turn. What is the result of this game?

puzzles.explanation: Black's king on h1 is not in check, but White's king covers g1 and g2 and the knight covers h2. Black has no legal move, so it is stalemate and the game is drawn.

puzzles.title: Piece Values · 1

exercise.prompt: A knight and a bishop together are worth about the same as which of these?

puzzles.explanation: A knight (3) and a bishop (3) make 6 points. A rook (5) and a pawn (1) also make 6. A queen is 9, and two pawns only 2.

puzzles.title: Piece Values · 2

exercise.prompt: White to move. Find the capture that wins material without losing the queen.

puzzles.explanation: The rook on a7 is worth five points and nothing guards it. Taking the pawn on d5 or g7 would cost the queen, worth nine, for one point.

puzzles.title: Counting Material · 1

exercise.prompt: Count the attackers. Choose every white piece that attacks the black pawn on e5.

puzzles.explanation: The knight on f3, the rook on e1 and the pawn on d4 all attack e5. The bishop on c1 and the queen on d1 do not reach it.

puzzles.title: Counting Material · 2
