exercise.prompt: Choose every black piece, apart from the king, that has no defender.

puzzles.explanation: The rook on a8, the knight on c6, the bishop on d6 and the pawn on b5 have no defender. The rook guards the pawn on a7, and the king guards f7, g7 and h7.

puzzles.title: Chess Notation · 1

exercise.prompt: What does the move Bxe5 mean?
choices: A bishop moves to e5 without capturing
A pawn on the b-file captures on e5
A bishop gives check on e5

puzzles.explanation: B is the bishop, x means a capture, and e5 is the square where the capture happens. A pawn capture would start with a small file letter, as in dxe5.

puzzles.title: Chess Notation · 2

exercise.prompt: White to play. Play the move written Rd8#.

puzzles.explanation: R is the rook, d8 is its target square and # means checkmate. The rook on d8 checks along the back rank and also covers f8 and h8, while Black's own pawns on f7, g7 and h7 block the king's way forward.

puzzles.title: Good Manners at the Board · 1

exercise.prompt: You touch your knight on purpose, and it has a legal move. Then you notice a better move with your bishop. What must you do?

puzzles.explanation: Touch-move: a piece of your own that you touch on purpose must be moved if it can move legally. Announcing an adjustment works only before touching, and only to straighten a piece.

puzzles.title: Good Manners at the Board · 2

exercise.prompt: Your opponent has just checkmated you. What is the polite thing to do?
choices: Ask to take back your last move

puzzles.explanation: Good players are gracious in defeat: shake hands, congratulate your opponent, and learn from the game.

puzzles.title: Playing in a Tournament · 1

exercise.prompt: You have just moved your bishop with your right hand. How should you press the clock?
choices: With either hand, whenever you like

puzzles.explanation: Use the hand that moved the piece to press the clock as well.

puzzles.title: Playing in a Tournament · 2

exercise.prompt: You think your opponent has just made an illegal move. What should you do?
choices: Pause the clock and call the arbiter
exercise.answer: Pause the clock and call the arbiter

puzzles.explanation: The arbiter settles disputes. Pause the clock and ask for the arbiter instead of arguing with your opponent.

puzzles.title: Rules Review · 1

exercise.prompt: White wants to castle, and neither the king nor the rooks have moved. Castle on the side where it is allowed.

puzzles.explanation: Black's bishop on c4 covers f1, which the king has to pass over to castle kingside, so that side is closed. Queenside castling works: the king goes from e1 to c1.

puzzles.title: Rules Review · 2

exercise.prompt: Black's pawn has just moved from d7 to d5. Find White's move that gives check.

puzzles.explanation: Capturing en passant, from e5 to d6, removes the pawn on d5, and the white pawn on d6 now attacks the king on c7.

puzzles.title: Opening Principles · 1

exercise.prompt: White to move. Castle to make the king safe.

puzzles.context: White has brought out a knight and both bishops, so f1 and g1 are empty.
puzzles.explanation: The king goes to g1 and the rook hops over to f1. On the other side the knight and queen still block the way, so only kingside castling is possible.

puzzles.title: Opening Principles · 2

exercise.prompt: Which is the best habit in the opening?
choices: Bring the queen out early and attack with her alone
Bring out knights and bishops, then castle
Move the same knight again and again
Push the pawns on the edge first
exercise.answer: Bring out knights and bishops, then castle

puzzles.explanation: Developing the knights and bishops and castling early gets your army ready and keeps your king safe.

puzzles.title: Scholar's Mate · 1

exercise.prompt: White to move. Find checkmate in one.

puzzles.context: Black has not protected the pawn on f7.
puzzles.explanation: The queen captures on f7. The bishop on c4 guards her, so the king cannot take, and the king has nowhere to go.

puzzles.title: Scholar's Mate · 2

exercise.prompt: Black to move. Find checkmate in one.

puzzles.context: White has spent the opening on pawn moves and left f2 guarded only by the king.
puzzles.explanation: The queen captures on f2, guarded by the bishop on c5, and it is checkmate. Taking with the bishop also mates, because then the queen guards f2.

puzzles.title: The Fork · 1

exercise.prompt: White to move. Find a knight fork.

puzzles.explanation: The knight jumps to c7. It checks the king on e8 and attacks the queen on a8, and nothing can capture it.

puzzles.title: The Fork · 2

exercise.prompt: White to move. Find a pawn fork.

puzzles.explanation: The pawn moves to d5 and attacks both knights. Neither knight can capture it, and only one can move away, so White wins a knight for at most a pawn.

puzzles.title: The Pin · 1

exercise.prompt: The bishop on b5 pins Black's c6 knight against the king. On which squares could that knight legally land? Mark them all, or none if it has no move.

puzzles.explanation: None. Any knight move would leave Black's king in check from the bishop on b5, and that is against the rules.

puzzles.title: The Pin · 2

exercise.prompt: The bishop on g5 pins Black's f6 knight against the queen, not the king. On which squares could that knight legally land? Mark them all, or none if it has no move.

puzzles.explanation: This is a relative pin, so every normal knight move is legal. Each one lets the bishop on g5 capture the queen on d8, though.

puzzles.title: The Skewer · 1

exercise.prompt: White to move. Give a check that skewers the king and the queen.

puzzles.context: Black's king and queen stand on the same rank.
puzzles.explanation: The rook moves to h6 and checks the king on d6. The king must leave the rank, and then the rook captures the queen on a6.

puzzles.title: The Skewer · 2

exercise.prompt: White to move. Give a check that skewers the king and the rook.

puzzles.context: Black's king on d5 and rook on g8 stand on the same diagonal.
puzzles.explanation: The bishop moves to b3 and checks the king. Once the king steps off the diagonal, the bishop captures the rook on g8.

puzzles.title: Discovered Attacks · 1

exercise.prompt: Find White's discovered check that also attacks two black pieces.

puzzles.context: White's bishop on b1 is lined up behind the pawn on d3.
puzzles.explanation: The pawn steps from d3 to d4. That uncovers the bishop on b1, which now checks the king on h7, and the pawn attacks both the queen on c5 and the knight on e5. Black must answer the check, and whatever Black does, White wins the queen: if the queen blocks on c2, the bishop takes it with check.

puzzles.title: Discovered Attacks · 2

exercise.prompt: Move the knight to uncover the bishop's check and give checkmate.

puzzles.context: Any other knight move gives only the bishop's check, and Black's rook could block it on g7.
puzzles.explanation: The knight jumps to f7 and checks the king on h8, and the bishop on b2 checks it too. Against a double check only the king can move, but g7 is guarded by the bishop and g8 and h7 hold Black's own pieces. Checkmate.

puzzles.title: Removing the Defender · 1

exercise.prompt: White's rook attacks the knight on d5. Which black pieces guard that knight? Pick every one.

puzzles.explanation: Two pieces guard d5: the pawn on c6, which captures diagonally forward onto d5, and the knight on f6. To win the knight on d5, White would first have to remove its guards.

puzzles.title: Removing the Defender · 2

exercise.prompt: Black's bishop on d5 is guarded only by the knight. Capture the guard without losing your piece.

puzzles.context: Taking on d5 first would cost the rook, because the knight on f6 guards that square.
puzzles.explanation: The bishop takes the knight on f6, and nothing can take it back. Now the bishop on d5 has lost its guard, and White's rook is ready to win it too.

puzzles.title: Two-Rook Checkmate · 1

exercise.prompt: One rook already holds the seventh rank. Give checkmate with the other.

puzzles.context: Moving the rook on a7 would open the seventh rank and let the king out.
puzzles.explanation: The rook goes to b8 and checks along the last rank. The rook on a7 still guards e7, f7 and g7, so Black's king has no square left. Checkmate.

puzzles.title: Two-Rook Checkmate · 2

exercise.prompt: The king is trapped against the side of the board. Find the checkmate.

puzzles.context: The rook on g1 holds the g-file like a wall.
puzzles.explanation: The rook slides along the second rank to h2 and checks up the h-file. The rook on g1 guards the whole g-file, so the king cannot step sideways. The ladder works towards a side edge too.

puzzles.title: Queen Checkmate · 1

exercise.prompt: The queen has built a box. Pick every square Black's king can move to.

puzzles.context: White's queen stands a knight's move from Black's king.
puzzles.explanation: The queen on e4 guards the e-file and the diagonal through f5 and g6, so the king can only go to f7, g5 or g7. All three are inside the box.

puzzles.title: Queen Checkmate · 2

exercise.prompt: Give checkmate, and take care not to stalemate the king.

puzzles.context: White's king on c7 already guards b7 and b8.
puzzles.explanation: The queen checks along the a-file from a6 or a3. White's king guards b7 and b8, and the queen guards a7, so it is checkmate. A queen move to b6 would be a mistake: the king would not be in check but would have no legal move, which is stalemate.

puzzles.title: Rook Checkmate · 1

exercise.prompt: The kings face each other. Give checkmate with the rook.

puzzles.explanation: The rook checks along the last rank from a8. White's king on f6 covers e7, f7 and g7, and the rook covers e8 and g8. Checkmate.

puzzles.title: Rook Checkmate · 2

exercise.prompt: Black's king is in the corner. Find the checkmate.

puzzles.context: A check from h7 would not be mate, because the king could escape to g8.
puzzles.explanation: The rook checks from b8 along the last rank. White's king on g6 covers g7 and h7, and the rook covers g8. Checkmate.

puzzles.title: Winning Material Puzzles · 1

exercise.prompt: White to move. Find the knight jump that attacks two black pieces at once.

puzzles.context: Black's queen on c6 attacks your knight on d5.
puzzles.explanation: The knight jumps to e7 with check and attacks the queen on c6 too. Black must move the king, and then the knight captures the queen.

puzzles.title: Winning Material Puzzles · 2

exercise.prompt: White to move. Several captures are possible. Find the only one that wins material safely.

puzzles.context: Black's bishop on g5 attacks your queen.
puzzles.explanation: The queen takes the bishop on g5, and nothing can take her back. The pawn on d5 is guarded by the queen and the knight, and the king guards f7.

puzzles.title: Mate in One Puzzles · 1

exercise.prompt: White to move. Find the checkmate in one move.

puzzles.context: Black's queen is attacking, but it is White's move.
puzzles.explanation: Rook to d8 is check along the back rank. The black pawns on f7, g7 and h7 hem in their own king, and nothing can block the check or capture the rook.

puzzles.title: Mate in One Puzzles · 2

exercise.prompt: White to move. Find the checkmate in one move.

puzzles.explanation: The queen moves to g7, right beside the king. White's king on f6 guards her, so the black king cannot take her, and she covers every square it could reach.

puzzles.title: A Famous Short Game · 1

exercise.prompt: This is the game just before White's eighth move. Find the castling move that brings White's rook to the d-file.

puzzles.context: Black's queen has just captured on e5.
puzzles.explanation: White castles queenside: the king goes to c1 and the rook to d1. The king is safer, and the rook joins the attack along the d-file.

puzzles.title: A Famous Short Game · 2

exercise.prompt: Black's king has just stepped to c7. Find White's checkmate.

puzzles.context: White has given up the queen and is far behind in material.
puzzles.explanation: The bishop moves to d8 and checks the king. The rook on d1 guards the bishop and covers d6 and d7, and Black's own pieces block the other squares.

puzzles.title: Safe captures

exercise.prompt: White to move. Find the capture that wins material without losing the capturing piece.

puzzles.explanation: The knight takes the bishop on h4, and no black piece can reach h4. The knight on c6 is guarded by the pawn on b7, and the knight on e5 is guarded twice.

puzzles.title: Forks

exercise.prompt: White to move. Find the pawn move that attacks two black pieces at once.

puzzles.explanation: The pawn moves to e5 and attacks both knights, on d6 and f6. No black piece can take the pawn, and no knight move gives check, so White wins a knight for at most a pawn.

puzzles.title: Mate in one

exercise.prompt: White to move. Find the checkmate in one move.

puzzles.context: Black's queen is aiming at your king's side.
puzzles.explanation: The knight jumps to f7 and checks the king. The king's own rook and pawns fill every square around it, and nothing can capture the knight. This is called a smothered mate.

puzzles.title: Defended pieces

exercise.prompt: Choose every black piece and pawn that has no defender.

puzzles.explanation: The bishop on f5 and the pawn on b7 have no defender. The knight guards the rook and the pawn on a7, the pawn on b7 guards the knight, and the king guards f7, g7 and h7.
